feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content shows real scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative with strong career progression at NACo and a well-aligned headline/profile.  
- Good credibility through concrete scale indicators: 10,000+ page site, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, analytics stack, studio buildout.  
- Writing is generally concise and professional, with strong domain fit for mission-driven, advocacy, and public-sector communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: e.g., traffic growth, email performance, engagement gains, efficiency improvements, cost savings, or adoption results from platform/governance changes.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to tighten structure and save space.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; choose one style for lists with/without the Oxford comma (“web, email, social and multimedia” vs “web, email, social, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, currently learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with slightly sharper positioning, one or two concrete signals of scale, and less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more modern phrasing.
- Lead with your senior value proposition and sector fit: digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Add one concrete scale cue from recent roles, such as enterprise web platforms, large publisher groups, or high-volume audience engagement.
- Tighten broad phrases like “workflows and systems” and “clear, accessible content” so they feel more distinctive.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and scalable editorial and governance systems. Brings deep experience in advocacy and public-sector communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating complex policy or technical topics into accessible, audience-focused content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “stakeholder coordination” repeat ideas already covered in Core Competencies and Soft Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-level strengths rather than repeating detailed skill categories listed elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use broader, leadership-level phrases and reduce tool/process detail already covered in Topline Skills and Technical + IT.
- Standardize wording for parallel structure; e.g., use noun phrases consistently.
- Consider a tighter version: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, insights & reporting • Content operations & systems architecture • Stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia production
- If space is tight, replace “Multi-channel communication” with “Cross-channel communications leadership” for stronger seniority and clearer phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header summary.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “Data analytics & reporting” repeat detail already covered more specifically in Topline Skills/Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around strategic ownership, platform outcomes, and 1–2 signature initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate bullets to 4–5 and use stronger verbs: “Built enterprise workflows, analytics, and governance systems to improve cross-channel coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Combine Drupal/CMS points: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits; provided front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for high-traffic public sites.”
- Keep AI search as the differentiator and add outcomes if possible: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.” Add metrics such as launch status, adoption, time saved, or engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and microsite work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let Projects hold specifics.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also echo the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize consulting ownership and current strategic advisory scope.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper impact summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to lead with highest-impact achievements: website migration, analytics stack expansion, in-house studio build, governance/operations.
- Make outcomes more concrete where possible: add launch timing, traffic/engagement lift, reporting efficiency, production cost savings, turnaround time, or stakeholder adoption.
- Tighten channel bullet: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials” rather than listing platforms generically.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Video-programming language overlaps with older NACo entries and Recent Projects; emphasize building the studio/capability, not recurring video production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level, with sharper verbs and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems point: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” echo the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; keep this entry focused on scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize leadership scope and strategic outcomes rather than repeating generic capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered editorial planning
- Consider swapping “Editorial systems and governance” to “Editorial governance and operating models” for a more senior, systems-level tone.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one proof point tied to recent work, e.g. “10,000+ page web modernization” or “communications systems supporting 50+ publishers,” rather than keeping all bullets purely generic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” substantially duplicate the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent platform leadership and execution themes rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations & workflow automation • SharePoint & Power Pages • Airtable systems • AI-enabled search experiences
- Prioritize recent, proven strengths first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and integrations since those are most supported by current/f recent roles.
- Drop “jQuery” here unless required for the target role; it feels dated and is better kept in Technical + IT if needed.
- Consider replacing “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” with “CMS Platforms, Integrations & Automation” for a sharper, more outcomes-oriented label.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value analytical leadership and optimization capabilities, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis, and dashboarding across GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, and Microsoft Clarity”
- Put the most strategic items first: KPI design, executive/leadership reporting, analytics strategy, optimization.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented phrase tied to recent work: “analytics infrastructure for enterprise web decision-making” or “insight generation for 10,000+ page web platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.
- Tool list also overlaps almost exactly with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and avoid listing basic production tasks without context.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more strategic phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio buildout and operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Consider swapping “Video production and editing” for “Advocacy video programming” or “Recurring multimedia content production” to better reflect impact shown in recent roles.
- Drop “virtual” if keeping “hybrid event delivery”; it’s implied and saves space.
- If space allows, add scale/context in adjacent experience bullets rather than here, e.g., studio buildout, recurring programming, or event support.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid near-identical wording here.
- “Studio operations” and “video production and editing” are also reinforced in Work Experience, so this section should stay sharper and more differentiated.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is the strongest and most recent platform, give it visual priority.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider signaling depth: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier instead of just names: “CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages if it was only lightly used; it can weaken the senior enterprise emphasis versus Drupal/SharePoint
- Keep this item platform-focused only; save modernization, integrations, and AI/search language for adjacent technical skills sections

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; consider merging or trimming one of the two
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles/projects, so avoid repeating extra Drupal detail here unless other platforms need balancing

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and, where possible, reflect tools actually used in recent roles/projects.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied delivery: “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Integrations.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, REST/API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- Consider grouping by function for scanability: “Front end: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery | Integrations: REST/API integrations, GTM | DevOps/edge: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add one recent proof point in adjacent experience/project bullets rather than here, e.g., custom Drupal front-end work, API-driven features, or deployment automation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Analytics/Optimization unless implementation is a core differentiator.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing systems you’ve actually used to build workflows.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by relevance/strength: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp
- If accurate, add light functional framing instead of a flat list: Workflow automation (Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier) • Project management (Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp) • Team collaboration (Slack, Microsoft Teams)
- If space allows, replace one or two lower-value tools with stronger specifics from recent work, e.g., “Airtable workflow design” or “cross-team planning systems”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they support the workflow-systems narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this should stay as a concise tools list and, if possible, signal level of use rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform names for readability: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope/usage context in brief: enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, member engagement
- Optional stronger version: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (email automation, newsletter distribution, member communications)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “tens of thousands,” or channel leadership language here; that impact is already covered well in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 experience entries.
- “Engagement” may overlap with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item platform-focused.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like setup for later NACo roles. Tighten it around foundational impact, team-building, and concrete outputs without repeating responsibilities already covered in 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Add measurable scope if available: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, email/social volume, or team size supported.
- Make actions more direct and concise: “Helped launch NACo’s first in-house digital team; improved workflows across web, email, social, and video; supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and weekly video updates; informally supervised a digital media associate.”
- If accurate, highlight a durable outcome: improved production speed, more consistent publishing, expanded in-house multimedia capacity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/building the format rather than scaling it.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; specify early-stage process building here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.”
- Add the standout digital contribution: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Condense the rest: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support research dissemination and member-facing communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outputs: number of episodes, audiences reached, projects supported, or types of materials produced.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is too broad and repeats themes covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here; later positions already show progression into team and platform leadership.
